findings.message: contains 1 line(s) longer than 500 characters (possible minified/obfuscated code)
findings.remediation: Review extremely long lines; they may contain hidden logic.
findings.impact: Extremely long lines hide obfuscated or minified code from human review.
findings.attack_vector: Lines > 500 chars — code is structured to evade visual inspection.
findings.risk_adjustment: No automatic downgrade: risk changes require explicit protective controls.

findings.message: uses string concatenation or char-code construction to hide keywords
findings.remediation: Use readable, explicit code patterns; avoid character-code obfuscation.
findings.impact: Character-code construction hides string literals from grep-based detection.
findings.attack_vector: String.fromCharCode() builds dangerous strings at runtime — evades static patterns.
findings.risk_adjustment: No automatic downgrade: risk changes require explicit protective controls.

findings.message: references 1 known high-risk or anonymous destination(s)
findings.remediation: Route all network traffic through allowlisted, authenticated endpoints only.
findings.impact: Requests to anonymous or high-risk destinations can disclose plugin data to an untrusted operator.
findings.attack_vector: Network URL matches a known paste, tunnel, webhook, or anonymous file-hosting service.
findings.risk_adjustment: No automatic downgrade: risk changes require explicit protective controls.

findings.message: invokes an operating-system process API (5 calls in this file)
findings.remediation: Require explicit user approval and use a fixed allowlisted command with bounded arguments.
findings.downgrade: Downgraded from high: no system-impact pattern matched near the call site.
findings.impact: Attackers can execute arbitrary OS commands on the host, leading to full system compromise.
findings.attack_vector: Plugin spawns a child process with attacker-controlled arguments; no user approval gate.
findings.risk_adjustment: Explicit risk (medium) set by caller; evidence-based risk adjustment skipped.

findings.message: writes to system directories or boot locations
findings.remediation: Restrict file writes to user-owned directories with explicit approval.
findings.impact: Writing to system directories or boot locations gives attackers persistent root-level access.
findings.attack_vector: File write to /etc/init.d, /Library/LaunchDaemons, or Program Files — survives reboots.
findings.risk_adjustment: No automatic downgrade: risk changes require explicit protective controls.
